settings.text:
The glass cutting table is one of the most important machines used in double-glazed glass production. With natural resources and non-renewable energy sources becoming increasingly limited over recent decades, the efficient use of resources has become one of humanity's major concerns.
Since the construction sector accounts for a significant share of energy consumption, one of the most effective ways to improve energy efficiency in buildings is to use double-glazed windows.
As demand for double-glazed doors and windows has increased, many factories specializing in double-glazed glass production have been established.
In this article, we introduce the overall double-glazing production process and explain the importance and applications of the glass cutting table.

settings.title: What Is Double-Glazed Glass?
settings.text:
Double-glazed glass is made by bonding two or more parallel glass panes together to form a sealed, impermeable unit.
The principle of double glazing is based on creating a uniform cavity filled with dry air or gas between two or more panes.
This sealed cavity is formed using a slim aluminium profile (spacer) filled with a moisture-absorbing desiccant.
As a result, heat transfer, cold transfer, and the penetration of external noise into a building are significantly reduced.
Injecting gas into this cavity turns double-glazed glass into an effective thermal and acoustic insulator.
The type of glass used depends on the intended purpose of the double-glazed window.
Therefore, the most important considerations are the glass type and the performance you expect from it:
1. If thermal insulation is your priority, the thermal performance can be improved by selecting thinner glass panes and a wider thermal spacer.
2. If acoustic insulation is your priority, thicker glass panes are generally required. Thicker panes disrupt sound waves more effectively and provide better sound insulation.
3. If both thermal and acoustic insulation are required, 4 mm and 6 mm glass panes can be used with an 8 mm air gap between them, resulting in a total thickness of 18 mm.

settings.title: How Is Double-Glazed Glass Manufactured in a Factory?
settings.text:
Double-glazed glass consists of three main components: two single glass panes and a thermal spacer placed between them.
Factories manufacture double-glazed glass using a dedicated production line.
First, the required glass dimensions are determined. The spacers are cut by a machine and the frame is prepared.
The glass panes are then cut using a glass cutting table and washed in a dedicated machine to remove even the smallest marks and stains.
Next, a sealing adhesive (usually polyisobutylene) is applied to both sides of the spacer, and the glass panes are bonded to it.
To fill the unit with gas, two holes are made in the spacer. Gas inlet and outlet hoses are connected to the double-glazed unit, which is then filled with gas.
Argon is generally used as the filling gas. A moisture-absorbing desiccant is used to remove moisture from the air trapped between the panes during production.

settings.title: Double-Glazed Glass Production Machinery
settings.text:
It is worth noting that double-glazed windows were invented in the 1930s and introduced to the market in the 1950s.
Over the past 50 years, double-glazing production methods have advanced considerably, and the insulating performance of these products has improved significantly.
Some of the equipment and machines used in double-glazed glass factories include:
Double-glazed glass washing machine
Double-glazed glass pressing table
Double-glazed glass cutting table
Double-glazed glass butyl applicator
Argon gas filling machine for double-glazed glass
Double-glazed glass sealant applicator
Ordinary glass can be cut easily using a diamond cutter. Its structure allows a localized break without damaging the entire pane; only the section being cut or broken is affected.
This is not the case with double-glazed glass, which requires specialized factory equipment for cutting, as explained in the following sections.

settings.title: Technical Specifications of the Glass Cutting Table
settings.text:
Since double-glazed glass is used in products such as building doors and windows, safety is essential.
The way double-glazed glass is cut and the use of correct cutting methods are among the most important aspects of its production process.
For this reason, professional cutting machines are essential in factories. This machine offers the following features and specifications:
• Ability to load and lift glass sheets measuring 3.21 × 2.25 m without manual handling
• Equipped with two powerful pneumatic jacks with a lifting capacity of 400 kg
• Air-cushion system for easy movement of glass across the table surface
• Equipped with two powerful blower motors to supply air to the table surface
• Table frame constructed using thick 80 × 40 mm industrial steel tubing
• Equipped with four swivel industrial wheels for easy table movement
• Special anti-scratch cutting carpet on the table surface
• Perforated grooves between the two layers of wooden board
• Option to install pneumatic arms on the table surface to separate cut glass sheets
• Uses premium-quality, standard-compliant components
• Counterweight system to prevent the table from tipping over
• Modern design and user-friendly operation
• Finished with electrostatic powder coating, oven-cured
• Includes an 18-month three-star Gold Warranty
• Includes after-sales service and the supply of parts and spare components for 360 months
